title: Mathematical facets — special values and derived-relation faces
description: Each entry is a Facet: one face a mathematical object presents at a chosen angle — a special function value, a ratio, or a limiting face — rather than a standalone constant. Where /2 (Structures) held the primary constants, /3 (Facets) holds the faces they show in identities and special cases.

provenance.primary_source: Standard mathematical definitions and identities (public domain)
provenance.cross_reference: OEIS — On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (A-numbers per entry); DLMF (NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions) for special values
provenance.note: Mathematical facets are definitional/derived, not measured; digits shown are truncated decimal expansions of exact objects. Facets and relation faces are alphabetized by name for reader ease.

facets.definition: common-log face of e (the change-of-base factor)
